ColumnBloomFilters

The columns that get a bloom filter in every row group, keyed by column path with dots (address.city). A bloom filter tells a reader that a value is certainly not in a row group (it is wrong the other way a small share of the time, see FalsePositiveRate), which the minimum and the maximum cannot when the values are spread widely, as ids and names are. Each takes room in the file, about a byte for every few different values. Hashing and counting the values makes writing the column several times slower when the pages are not compressed, and little slower when they are. Booleans and INT96 cannot have one.

public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, BloomFilterSettings>? ColumnBloomFilters { get; init; }

Reported when the writer is created: a column that does not exist or cannot have a filter, or settings that make no sense.

ColumnDictionaries

How chosen columns are dictionary encoded, keyed by column path with dots (scores.list.element): the DictionaryMode and the size limit of the dictionary, in place of DictionaryPageSizeLimit. The others use Standard and the limit of the writer. A DictionaryMode can be given where settings are expected. Nothing here makes a column use a dictionary when DictionaryEnabled is off.

public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, DictionarySettings>? ColumnDictionaries { get; init; }

Reported when the writer is created: a column that does not exist, or a size limit below 1.

ColumnEncodings

The encoding to use for the values of chosen columns, keyed by column path with dots (scores.list.element). The default is PLAIN. A column chosen here uses its encoding for every page that is not dictionary encoded: all of them when DictionaryEnabled is off, otherwise the pages after the dictionary is given up. DELTA_BINARY_PACKED suits integers that change steadily, DELTA_LENGTH_BYTE_ARRAY and DELTA_BYTE_ARRAY strings (the latter when they share prefixes), and BYTE_STREAM_SPLIT floating-point numbers before compression.

public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ParquetEncoding>? ColumnEncodings { get; init; }

Compression

How pages are compressed. The codec must be available in Codecs; Snappy, Zstd and LZ4_RAW come from add-on packages and have to be registered first. Defaults to no compression.

DataPageSize

The size, in bytes of encoded values before compression, at which a data page is closed. Smaller pages allow finer-grained reading, larger ones spend less on headers. A single value bigger than this still gets a page of its own. Defaults to 1 MiB.

public int DataPageSize { get; init; }

Property Value

int

DataPageVersion

The layout of the data pages. Defaults to V1, which every reader understands; V2 stores the levels uncompressed and compresses only the values.

public DataPageVersion DataPageVersion { get; init; }

DataPageVersion

DictionaryEnabled

Whether columns are dictionary encoded: each distinct value is stored once and the rows refer to it by number, which is far smaller for repetitive data. A column falls back to plain encoding once its dictionary grows past DictionaryPageSizeLimit. Booleans are never dictionary encoded. Defaults to true.

public bool DictionaryEnabled { get; init; }

Property Value

bool

DictionaryPageSizeLimit

The size, in bytes, a column chunk's dictionary may reach before the writer stops adding to it and falls back to plain encoding for the rest of the chunk. Defaults to 1 MiB. The size is checked after every page worth of values (and after every batch written), so a dictionary can overshoot the limit by up to that much.

public int DictionaryPageSizeLimit { get; init; }

Property Value

int

StatisticsEnabled

Whether the minimum, maximum and null count of every column chunk are recorded in the footer, which lets readers skip data that cannot match a filter. Costs a pass over the values. Defaults to true.

StatisticsTruncateLength

The longest minimum or maximum, in bytes, kept for string and binary columns. Longer ones are shortened to a bound (a prefix for a minimum, an increased prefix for a maximum) and marked as not exact. Defaults to 64.

public int StatisticsTruncateLength { get; init; }

Property Value

int

WritePageChecksums

Whether the header of every page carries the CRC-32 of the page as it is written (after compression), so that a reader can tell that the bytes were damaged. Computing it costs about 1 second per GB of page bytes: noticeable (tens of percent) when writing uncompressed pages, negligible next to a compression codec. Off by default.

public bool WritePageChecksums { get; init; }

Property Value

bool

WritePageIndex

Whether the file gets a page index: for every column, where each data page is and the smallest and largest value in it, written after the row groups. A reader that is given a condition can then skip the pages that cannot hold a row that satisfies it, not only the row groups, which pays off in row groups of many pages whose values are in some order (a time, an id that grows). The index takes a few bytes a page and the bounds cost a little time to collect. Needs StatisticsEnabled for the bounds; without it only the positions of the pages are written. Off by default.

public bool WritePageIndex { get; init; }

Property Value

bool
